newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Aviatrans to resume Moscow-Verona charters.
newsitem.headline: Russian Aviatrans to resume Moscow-Verona charters.

text.p: Russia's Atran-Aviatrans cargo airline plans to restart charters flights as early as next month between Moscow and Verona in Italy, its commercial director said on Monday.
Alexander Seryan told Reuters that flights were postponed last month because the airline changed its name and Italian authorities required it to submit a series of new documents.

"We have finished registration of a new name -- Atran-Aviatrans Cargo Airlines -- and hope to re-start charters to Italy, operating Ilyushin-76 and Antonov-12 planes," Seryan said. "We do not have problems with Italian aviation authorities to resume these flights."

Private Atran-Aviatrans carrier was founded in 1990 and it now operates eight Ilyushin-76, three Antonov-32, six An-26 and eight An-12 freighters, making charters from Moscow to 132 destinations around the world, including 70 destinations in Europe.

Last October a giant Antonov-124 freighter owned by another carrier, Ayaks, crashed at Turin airport, which prompted Italy to bar Ayaks and several other small airlines from flying there. The accident killed the two-member crew and two villagers buried in rubble after the plane sliced into the village of San Francesco al Campo on a flight from Moscow.
The suspension of flights by Atran-Aviatrans last month was not related to this accident, Seryan said.
